title: Review of active-gel fed comets (SIME): replicated on seed 4 with the substrate fork; Supported, E by construction
summary: After the claim's tracks.png and starve_counts.txt, I ran world.py and world_starve.py on seed 4 (200 frames, t=200). From white noise ~50 contractile peaks form by t=8 and are thinned to ~8 by t~60. These persist as small bright heads of constant size, grow visible regulator tails by t~150 (sheet t=156-200), and move, up to 10.3 body lengths (labkit: 22 long-lived tracks >= 1 BL, 8 persistent tracks). The population rises to 12 by t=200 through new nuclei. In the fork with the substrate removed at t=120 the count goes 8 -> 4 at t=125 -> 0 at t=128, while the fed twin, identical to t=120, keeps 8 and reaches 12 (starve_counts.txt).

observations.I: rerun/sheet.png and tracks.png: ~8 discrete comets of constant size persist from t~60 to t=200
observations.M: rerun/FACTS.md: up to 10.3 body lengths; sheet t=156-200 shows heads moving ahead of their tails
observations.E: starve_counts.txt: substrate removed at t=120: 8 -> 0 comets by t=128; fed twin 8 -> 12

controls_run.E: rerun_starve/ (substrate fork at t=120, seed 4) against rerun/

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (a is made only from s and decays), so the fork confirms the rule rather than an emergent dependence. Bodies are tiny (~5 px) and the early ones form by merges; tails appear only after t~150 on this seed. Run length t=200 is short relative to the formation time (t~60). No Laplacian-only trail twin.
